title: SoftGlaze AI
description: Let AI apps like Claude, Cursor and ChatGPT work with your profiles. Every change asks you first, and everything is logged.
copyFailed: Could not copy. Select the text and copy it by hand.

states.unavailableTitle: SoftGlaze AI is not available in this build
states.unavailableBody: This version of SoftGlaze Browser does not include the AI server yet. It comes with an update. Nothing is wrong with your workspace.
states.forbiddenTitle: Only the Owner or an Admin can manage SoftGlaze AI
states.forbiddenBody: Ask the workspace Owner for access. When an AI app uses a token that acts as you, its requests still pop up for you to allow or deny, on any page.

stop.title: Stop all AI?
stop.body: Use this if an AI app is doing something you did not expect.
stop.point1: Every run and profile an AI app started stops now.
stop.point2: Every connected AI app is disconnected, and calls in progress are cancelled.
stop.point3: Every request waiting for your answer is denied.
stop.point4: SoftGlaze AI is switched off. Tokens stay valid; turn it on again when you are ready.
stop.result: Done. Runs stopped: {{runs}}. Profiles stopped: {{profiles}}. Calls cancelled: {{calls}}. Sessions ended: {{sessions}}. Requests denied: {{approvals}}.
stop.nowOff: SoftGlaze AI is off. AI apps cannot connect until you turn it on.

start.title: Get started in three steps
start.step2: Create a token for your AI app

connect.emptyOn: The AI server sent no setup. Try Refresh.
connect.emptyBody: Turn on the AI server to see how to connect each app.
connect.placeholderHint: <YOUR_TOKEN> is where your token goes. You see a token only once, when you create it.

envVar.title: Save the token for Codex
envVar.body: Codex reads the token from an environment variable named SOFTGLAZE_TOKEN. Run this once with your token, then open a new terminal.
envVar.unix: macOS or Linux (add it to your shell profile)

bridge.title: Bridge for apps that start a local program
bridge.body: Some apps cannot connect to a web address. They start the SoftGlaze bridge instead, and the bridge passes everything to the AI server on this PC. Same token, same approvals.
bridge.unavailable: The bridge is not included in this build.
bridge.mcpb: One-click install file for Claude Desktop

claude-desktop.title: Claude Desktop
claude-desktop.step1: Create a token for Claude Desktop with the button below.
claude-desktop.step2: Easiest: install the SoftGlaze.mcpb file shown below (Settings > Extensions > Advanced settings > Install Extension) and enter your token when Claude asks. Or open Settings > Developer > Edit Config and paste the setup into claude_desktop_config.json, with your token in place of <YOUR_TOKEN>.
claude-desktop.step2NoMcpb: Open Settings > Developer > Edit Config and paste the setup into claude_desktop_config.json, with your token in place of <YOUR_TOKEN>. It starts the SoftGlaze bridge, because Claude Desktop runs local servers.
claude-desktop.step3: Quit and reopen Claude Desktop. SoftGlaze shows up under the + button below the chat box, in Connectors.

claude-code.title: Claude Code
claude-code.step1: Create a token for Claude Code with the button below.
claude-code.step2: Run the command in a terminal, with your token in place of <YOUR_TOKEN>.
claude-code.step3: Start Claude Code and type /mcp. SoftGlaze should show as connected.

cursor.title: Cursor
cursor.step1: Create a token for Cursor with the button below.
cursor.step2: Open ~/.cursor/mcp.json (or .cursor/mcp.json in one project) and paste the setup, with your token in place of <YOUR_TOKEN>.
cursor.step3: In Cursor's settings, check that SoftGlaze is listed and switched on. Then ask the chat to list your SoftGlaze profiles.

vscode.title: VS Code (Copilot)
vscode.step1: Create a token for VS Code with the button below.
vscode.step2: Add the setup to .vscode/mcp.json in your workspace (or run MCP: Open User Configuration). The first time SoftGlaze starts, VS Code asks for your token and stores it securely, so it never sits in the file.
vscode.step3: Open Copilot Chat and ask it to list your SoftGlaze profiles. Allow the tool when VS Code asks.

gemini-cli.title: Gemini CLI
gemini-cli.step1: Create a token for Gemini CLI with the button below.
gemini-cli.step2: Add the setup inside "mcpServers" in ~/.gemini/settings.json, with your token in place of <YOUR_TOKEN>. Leave "trust" off: SoftGlaze asks you before every change anyway.
gemini-cli.step3: Start gemini and type /mcp. SoftGlaze and its tools should be listed.

codex.title: ChatGPT desktop / Codex
codex.step1: Create a token for Codex with the button below, then save it in the SOFTGLAZE_TOKEN environment variable (command below).
codex.step2: Add the setup to ~/.codex/config.toml. Codex reads the token from SOFTGLAZE_TOKEN, so the file never holds it.
codex.step3: Open a new terminal, start Codex and type /mcp. SoftGlaze should be listed.

windsurf.title: Windsurf
windsurf.step1: Create a token for Windsurf with the button below.
windsurf.step2: Paste the setup into Windsurf's MCP config file (see Where it goes), with your token in place of <YOUR_TOKEN>.
windsurf.step3: Refresh the MCP servers in Windsurf and check that SoftGlaze is listed.

cline.title: Cline
cline.step1: Create a token for Cline with the button below.
cline.step2: In Cline, open MCP Servers > Configure and paste the setup into cline_mcp_settings.json, with your token in place of <YOUR_TOKEN>.
cline.step3: Check that SoftGlaze shows as connected in Cline's MCP Servers list.

other.title: Other apps
other.step1: Create a token for the app with the button below.
other.step2: Open the app's MCP settings and add a server with this address and an Authorization header: Bearer, a space, then your token.
other.step3: If the app can only start a local program (stdio), use the SoftGlaze bridge below instead of the address.

custom.step1: Create a token for this app with the button below.
custom.step2: Paste the setup where the app keeps its MCP servers, with your token in place of <YOUR_TOKEN>.
custom.step3: Restart the app and check that SoftGlaze is listed in its MCP or tools settings.

n8n.subtitle: Run SoftGlaze from n8n workflows on this PC.
n8n.selfHosted: n8n must run on this PC (npx or Docker). n8n Cloud cannot reach your PC yet.
n8n.noPort: Turn on the AI server to see the n8n address.

a.title: Let an n8n AI Agent use SoftGlaze
a.step1: Add an AI Agent node, then add an MCP Client Tool node as one of its tools.
a.step2: Set SSE Endpoint to the address below. If n8n runs in Docker, use the Docker address.
a.step3: Set Authentication to Bearer and paste your token. Under Tools to Include, pick All or only the tools you need.
a.dockerNote: For Docker, also add host.docker.internal under Extra allowed host names on the Settings tab.

b.title: Fixed steps with the HTTP Request node
b.body: For steps that never change, such as starting one profile at 9:00, an HTTP Request node can call the Local API directly. Send the token in the Authorization header.

c.title: Use an Automation token for scheduled workflows
c.body: A workflow that runs on a schedule has nobody to click Allow. An Automation token pre-approves only the tools you pick, only for the groups you pick, with limits per call and per hour. Everything else still asks.
c.ownerOnly: Only the Owner can create Automation tokens.

read.title: Read only
read.body: Can look at profiles, proxies, groups and activity. Cannot change or start anything.

operate.title: Operate
operate.body: Can also create and start profiles, run macros and work inside pages. Changes still ask you first, as set in Settings.

full.title: Full
full.body: Everything in Operate, plus expert tools when Expert mode is on. Only for apps you fully trust.

create.title: Create a token
create.description: A token lets one AI app connect. It acts as a member of your team and can only do what that member may do.
create.revealDescription: Copy it into your AI app now.
create.name: Name
create.nameHint: Say which app and which computer, so you can recognise it later.
create.memberHint: The AI works as this member, with this member's permissions and profiles.
create.expiryNeverWarn: A token that never expires stays valid until you revoke it.
create.profilesAllHint: Every profile the member can open.
create.profilesSomeHint: Only profiles in the groups you tick.
create.noGroups: There are no groups yet. Create one on the Groups page first.
create.onceWarning: Copy this token now. SoftGlaze shows it only this once. If you lose it, revoke it and create a new one.
create.filledSetup: Setup for {{app}}, with your token filled in
create.n8nHint: In n8n, set Authentication to Bearer and paste this token.
create.acknowledge: I have saved this token somewhere safe
create.closeWarning: Copy the token or tick the box first. You cannot see this token again.

errors.nameTooLong: Keep the name to {{max}} characters or fewer.
errors.scopeRequired: Choose what the token may do.
errors.groupsRequired: Tick at least one group, or choose All.
errors.groupsRequiredAutomation: An Automation token must be limited to groups. Tick at least one group.
errors.toolNotAllowed: One of the tools cannot be pre-approved.
errors.limitRange: Enter a whole number from {{min}} to {{max}}.
errors.noToken: The AI server did not return a token. Try again.

automation.title: Automation token (for n8n, schedules and scripts)
automation.intro: For workflows that run without you, pick the tools that may run without asking.
automation.needsOperate: Choose Operate or Full above to pre-approve tools.
automation.warning: These tools will run without asking you. They stay limited to the chosen groups, are logged, and stop with Stop all AI.
automation.groupsNote: Pre-approved tools only work on the groups ticked under Profiles it may use. Every other tool still asks you.

tools.update_profile: Change a profile (name, group, tags, notes, start page, proxy)
tools.rotate_proxy_ip: Get a new IP from the proxy
tools.page_press_key: Press a key on a page
tools.page_wait_for: Wait for something on a page

tokens.intro: Each AI app connects with its own token. A token acts as one member and can be limited to some groups. Revoke a token to cut that app off at once.
tokens.emptyBody: Create a token, then paste it into your AI app. The Connect tab shows where it goes.
tokens.caption: AI tokens
tokens.revokeBody: The AI app using this token loses access right away. This cannot be undone.

approval.title: {{app}} is asking for permission
approval.timeLeft: left to answer. With no answer, the request is denied.
approval.timeLeftHint: Time left before the request is denied
approval.timeLeftSr: {{time}} left before the request is denied
approval.secondsLeftAnnounce: {{seconds}} seconds left to answer the AI request
approval.noArgs: This request has no extra details.
approval.redactedNote: Passwords and other secrets are hidden here.
approval.allowHourHint: Do not ask again for this kind of action from {{token}} for the next hour.
approval.footnote: SoftGlaze asks inside the app, whatever the AI app's own settings say. Every answer is logged under Activity.
approval.later: Decide later (it is denied when time runs out)
approval.timedOut: The request from {{app}} timed out and was denied.
approval.gone: That request was already answered or cancelled.

approvals.intro: Every action that changes something waits here until you answer. A request with no answer is denied after 2 minutes. The same request also pops up on any page.
approvals.emptyBody: When an AI app wants to change something, the request appears here and as a pop-up on any page.

activity.noMatchBody: Try another result, app or search.
activity.emptyBody: Everything an AI app does through SoftGlaze is listed here: what it asked for, your answer and how it went.
activity.caption: AI activity

memory.title: Workspace memory
memory.description: Notes every AI app reads before it starts: how you name things, what each group is for, proxy rules, working hours and what it must never do. Plain Markdown.
memory.placeholder: Write notes for AI apps here, in Markdown.
memory.over: That is over the limit. Shorten it to save.
memory.tip: Tip: press Ctrl+S to save. Keep it short and specific: AI apps read all of it every time.
memory.guidesDescription: SoftGlaze gives every AI app these guides too. They are read-only.
memory.resetTitle: Reset the memory to the default?
memory.resetBody: Your notes are replaced with the SoftGlaze template. This cannot be undone.

howItWorks.title: How SoftGlaze works
howItWorks.body: Profiles, fingerprints, proxies, groups, sessions, macros and plan limits, and how to use the tools well.

acceptableUse.title: Acceptable use
acceptableUse.body: What SoftGlaze may and may not be used for. AI apps are told to refuse anything prohibited.

memory.guideReadOnly: Read-only. Kept up to date by SoftGlaze.

prompts.emptyBody: Ready-made prompts appear here when the AI server is available.
prompts.howIntro: Prompts are ready-made tasks. Your AI app fills in the details and carries them out with SoftGlaze.
prompts.howClaudeCode: type / and pick a softglaze prompt.
prompts.howClaudeDesktop: click + below the chat box and look for SoftGlaze.
prompts.howVsCode: type / in Copilot Chat and pick a SoftGlaze prompt.
prompts.howCursor: if prompts are not listed, copy the text below.
prompts.howOther: Any app: copy the prompt text, paste it into the chat and fill in the details.

settings.ownerOnlyHint: Only the workspace Owner can change this.

approvals.title: When SoftGlaze asks you
approvals.description: SoftGlaze asks inside the app before an AI app does something, whatever the AI app's own settings say.

read.title: Read-only tools
read.body: Looking at profiles, proxies, groups and activity.

operate.title: Operate tools
operate.body: Creating and starting profiles, running macros, working inside pages.

full.title: Full tools
full.body: Expert tools, only when Expert mode is on.

approvals.alwaysAsk: Some actions always ask every time, such as starting or stopping many profiles at once, and expert tools.

domains.title: Sites the AI may work on
domains.description: Page tools (open a page, click, type, read text) only work on the sites in this list and their subdomains.
domains.invalid: Enter a site name like example.com.
domains.empty: No sites yet. Page tools may open any site, and you are still asked first.

hosts.title: Extra allowed host names
hosts.description: The AI server only answers requests addressed to 127.0.0.1. For n8n or other tools running in Docker, add host.docker.internal.
hosts.invalid: Enter a host name like host.docker.internal, with no port or path.

expert.title: Expert mode
expert.description: Lets an AI app take over a running profile with Playwright, Puppeteer or Chrome DevTools.
expert.warning: Detectable. Outside tools control the browser in a way websites can spot, so profiles may be flagged or blocked. Off by default. Owner only.
expert.isOn: On. AI apps with a Full token can ask to take over a running profile. Each time asks you.
expert.isOff: Off. No AI app can take over a running profile.
expert.confirmBody: AI apps with a Full token can then ask to control running profiles directly. Websites can detect this, and accounts in those profiles may be flagged.
expert.ack: I understand that this can be detected and may get profiles flagged.

port.title: Server port
port.description: AI apps connect to http://127.0.0.1 on this port.
port.label: Port
port.hint: After you change it, update the address in every connected AI app. The Connect tab shows the new setup.
